text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bahraini press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Work is completed on seven new schools built at a cost of 5.5 million dinars in Bahrain.
- Labour ministry launches a campaign to bring down the country's level of unemployment which stood at 1.3 percent in July this year. The number of job seekers registered by the ministry was 3,606.
- Total trade between Bahrain and the United States fell in the first five months of 1997. U.S. exports to Bahrain dropped 16.8 percent and its imports also went down.
- Share trading at the Bahrain Stock Exchange reached new heights on Wednesday. The index climbed 29 points to close at 1,866.42 points.
- Bahrain-based United Gulf Bank posts a net profit of $16.3 million during the first half of this year, up from $5.2 million a year earlier.
- Gulf Arab states plan to set up a joint commercial firm to market products of small- and medium-sized industries, a Bahraini businessman says.
- Two Bahrainis killed when fire gutted their house in Bahrain on Wednesday.
- Bahrain's imports of perfume were worth seven million dinars in the first half of 1997, up from 5.6 million dinars in 1996.
